I'll help analyze the number of chemically equivalent carbon environments in the compound. Let me first get the 13C NMR spectrum data.

Looking at the 13C NMR spectrum, I can see 6 distinct chemical shift signals:
1. 168.60 ppm
2. 143.85 ppm
3. 130.30 ppm
4. 22.80 ppm
5. 21.35 ppm
6. 19.20 ppm

Each distinct signal in the 13C NMR spectrum represents a unique carbon environment (chemically non-equivalent carbons). Since we have 6 different chemical shifts, this means there are 6 different types of chemically equivalent carbon atoms in the compound.
